Various species of the genus Calodiscus Howell, 1935 are known from the Lower Cambrian of many regions of the world. They are found in China (Bergstrom at al., 2014), in Western Europe in Germany (Elicki and Schneider, 1992; Geyer and Elicki, 1995; Geyer at al., 2014), France (Howell, 1935), Sweden (Ahlberg and Bergstrom, 1993; Cederström et al., 2009), England (Hinz, 1987), Morocco (Geyer, 1988; Geyer and Landing, 1995), the USA (Rasetti, 1967), Canada (Westrop and Landing, 2011) and Greenland (Blaker and Peel, 1997). They are confined to the middle part of the Lower Cambrian and have a relatively narrow stratigraphic interval. Hence, representatives of the genus are considered as potential markers for the lower boundary of the fourth stage of the new International Stratigraphic Scale of the Cambrian System, which is currently being developed. Therefore, the study of species of this genus from Siberia is a high-priority task.

The genus Calodiscus was established by Howell (1935), with Agnostus lobatus Hall, 1847 designated as the type species. A total of about 20 species have been described or transferred from other genera. On the Siberian Platform, trilobites of the genus Calodiscus are known from eight localities (Figs. 1, 2) and are confined to the basal horizons of the Lower Cambrian Botomian Stage of the Russian General Stratigraphic Scale (GSS). To date, the following species of Calodiscus have been described from here: C. granulosus Jegorova et Shabanov, 1972, C. resimus Repina, 1972, C. schucherii (Matthew, 1896) and C. helena (Walcott, 1889). C. granulosus and C. resimus are endemic, they are found only on the Siberian Platform. C. schucherii and C. helena are also found in other regions.

In this paper, the morphology of representatives of the genus Calodiscus from the Lower Cambrian of the Siberian Platform is analyzed, since the authors’ preliminary assessments cast doubt on the taxonomic composition of the genus.

Abstract
Trilobites of the genus Calodiscus Howell, 1935 from the Lower Cambrian of the Siberian Platform are revised. ## Taxonomy

The probable ancestors of the Calodiscidae are among the Tsunyidiscidae. The Calodiscidae had no descendants.

## Description

Like all Agnostida, the Calodiscidae are diminutive and the headshield (or cephalon) and tailshield (or pygidium) are of approximately the same size (or isopygous) and outline. The central raised area of the cephalon (or glabella) has parallel sides or tapers forward, the front being rounded and expanded, and may be divided by transverse glabellar furrows. The occipital ring is defined by a complete transverse furrow and is neither spinose nor expanded. When present, the eye lobes are short and prominent. The thorax is only known in *Chelediscus* (two segments) and *Sinodiscus* (three segments). The pygidium has a wide, tapering axis of less than six segments.

Upper lower Cambrian (provisional Cambrian Series 2) trilobites are described from three sections through the Shuangyingshan Formation in the Beishan area, northwestern Gansu Province, China. Eleven species are described, of which seven are identified with previously described taxa and four described under open nomenclature. The composition of the fauna suggests biogeographic affinity with Siberian rather than Gondwanan trilobite faunas, and the Cambrian Series 2 faunas described herein and from elsewhere in northwestern China seem to be indicative of the marginal areas of the Siberian palaeocontinent.
